q: Kelp can look like an underwater tree. What kind of organism is it?
explain: Despite its leafy look, kelp isn't a plant at all. It's a large brown alga, grouped with the other algae we call seaweeds.
searchNote: Search summary attributed to this page the statement that kelp are not plants; they are grouped within the algae (the seaweeds) and are brown algae.

q: Which pigment gives kelp its golden-brown color?
explain: Kelp has chlorophyll like other photosynthesizers, but a pigment called fucoxanthin masks the green and gives it its brown tint.
searchNote: Search summary said kelp are brown algae in the order Laminariales whose color comes from the pigment fucoxanthin. The summary did not name the page for this sentence explicitly; the Smithsonian kelp page was the top result. Verifier: confirm fucoxanthin is on this page, and that the 'masks the green' wording is supported, or trim the explanation.

q: What is the main job of a kelp's holdfast, the root-like part at its base?
choices: Storing gas to float the blades
Gripping rock to anchor the kelp
explain: The holdfast's finger-like grips cling to rock and anchor the kelp. Unlike a plant root, it doesn't take up nutrients.

source2.title: Marine Plants / Algae - Point Reyes National Seashore (U.S. National Park Service)

searchNote: Monterey Bay Aquarium bull kelp page describes the holdfast as a root-like structure with finger-like projections that grip rock. An NPS page in the results says holdfasts work somewhat like roots but do not absorb nutrients (the summary did not say which NPS page; Point Reyes or Glacier Bay kelp-forest page are the candidates).

q: What do the gas-filled bladders on kelp, called pneumatocysts, do?
choices: Keep the blades floating near the surface
explain: These little gas-filled floats lift the kelp's blades up toward the sunlit surface, where they can photosynthesize.

source.title: Marine Plants / Algae - Point Reyes National Seashore (U.S. National Park Service)

searchNote: Search summary: pneumatocysts are gas-filled bladders that provide buoyancy and hold the blades near the surface; blades are where photosynthesis happens (NPS Point Reyes).

q: How does bull kelp hold its blades up near the surface?
choices: With one large float at the top of its stalk
With a small float at the base of every blade
With hollow blades filled with oil
explain: Bull kelp carries a single big gas bladder topped with a cluster of blades. Giant kelp, by contrast, has a small float at the base of each blade.

source.title: Marine Plants / Algae - Point Reyes National Seashore (U.S. National Park Service)

searchNote: NPS Point Reyes: giant kelp has one pneumatocyst on each blade, while bull kelp has a single pneumatocyst supporting many blades. Monterey Bay Aquarium: bull kelp's canopy sits at the top, while giant kelp has blades along the whole stipe.

q: The gas inside a bull kelp's float can be up to 10 percent of which gas?
explain: Surprisingly, the gas in a bull kelp's float can be up to 10 percent carbon monoxide, a byproduct the kelp produces itself.
searchNote: Monterey Bay Aquarium bull kelp page says the gas in the pneumatocyst can contain up to 10 percent carbon monoxide (the search summary said the page links it to photosynthesis). No second source was found. Verifier: confirm the exact figure and whether the page says 'byproduct'.

q: Bull kelp can grow from a microscopic spore into a towering adult in about how long?
explain: Bull kelp is an annual: it goes from spore to full size within one year, and the Smithsonian says it lives at most about 18 months.
searchNote: Monterey Bay Aquarium: bull kelp grows from a spore to maturity within a single year. Smithsonian Ocean: bull kelp are annuals, living a maximum of 18 months.

q: Under ideal conditions, giant kelp can grow up to about how much in a single day?
explain: In good conditions giant kelp can add roughly two feet (about 60 cm) a day, though its usual pace is slower.

q: In Alaska's kelp forests, what tends to happen when sea otters disappear?
choices: Kelp grows so thick that fish leave
Seals move in and eat the kelp
Urchins multiply and graze the kelp away
explain: Sea otters eat sea urchins. Without otters, urchins can mow down a kelp forest and leave a bare 'urchin barren' behind.

source2.publisher: NOAA Office of National Marine Sanctuaries
source2.title: Wildlife Health at Monterey Bay National Marine Sanctuary

searchNote: Smithsonian Ocean: otters keep Alaskan kelp forests balanced; without them urchins would mow down the kelp and an 'urchin barren' would emerge. NOAA Monterey Bay: when sea otters decline, urchin numbers explode and impact kelp. A 2024 PNAS study notes the effect is weaker in some places (San Nicolas Island), so the question is limited to Alaska and says 'tends to'.

q: Which sea star is considered a keystone predator of West Coast kelp forests because it eats several sea urchins a day?
explain: The sunflower sea star can eat several urchins a day, which helps keep urchins from overgrazing the kelp along the West Coast.

source.publisher: NOAA Office of National Marine Sanctuaries
source.title: Restoring Balance: What Sea Urchins Reveal About Ecosystem Health

searchNote: NOAA page says sunflower sea stars are considered a keystone predator essential for the survival of kelp forests along the West Coast because they can consume several urchins per day. Distractors are tropical Indo-Pacific species that do not live in West Coast kelp forests.

q: Algin, a substance extracted from kelp, is added to foods like ice cream for what purpose?
explain: Algin from kelp helps thicken, bind and stabilize foods and cosmetics, from ice cream to toothpaste.

source2.title: Sign: Kelp Forest (U.S. National Park Service)
